answer.rationale: The 2-hour-old release is the most actionable single intervention. Memory b1 documents a nearly identical pattern: a recent release caused a write-path error spike, and rollback restored stability without customer impact. Memory b6 confirms that canary/staged gating can catch bad builds, but here the release has already passed gates and reached production during peak settlement traffic—rollback is the fastest way to restore write-path latency. Memory b3 reminds us that capacity headroom can absorb surges, but the 5x latency climb correlates temporally with the release, not with a sudden traffic change (settlement peak is daily and expected), making rollback higher-leverage than add_capacity. Rolling back preserves in-flight writes (the prior build is stable per b1) and avoids the risk of regional failover or circuit breakers disrupting settlement-path transactions at peak. Read-replica routing (b5) addresses read load, not write-path latency, so it is not applicable here.
